stem: Chirag explores the diagram of rectangle $WXYZ$. He wants to study its diagonals by length and by the angles they make.

parts.text: Which claim correctly says which corners to join and what to compare?

options.text: Join opposite corners $W$ to $Y$ and $X$ to $Z$, then compare those diagonal lengths and the angles they form.
Join adjacent corners $W$ to $X$ only, because a diagonal is any side of the rectangle.
Join $W$ to $Z$ alone and call that the only diagonal, reversing which corners count as opposite.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Diagonals join opposite corners, so WY and XZ are the diagonals to measure and compare for length and angles.

teacher.key_rationale: Diagonals join opposite corners W–Y and X–Z; compare those lengths and angles. Joining only an adjacent side omits the opposite-corner condition. Treating WZ alone as the only diagonal reverses opposite pairing.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite/grid as rectangle WXYZ with both dashed diagonals drawn.
